subject: NexaHealth: proposed blended pricing & route add — next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up — token mix & target $/1M for Q3 expansion

Hi Paul — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Current ask: Nexa is planning a phased expansion in Q3 that adds a new route for clinical documentation (longform chat) while increasing existing summary/triage traffic (shorter chat + embeddings). You estimated a steady-state of ~80M tokens/month within 3 months of rollout, with a near-term ramp in month 1-2.

2) Unit-econ goals: you mentioned a target blended cost target of ~$950–1,100 per 1M tokens for the combined workload (priority on latency for clinical routes).

3) Our proposal items (attached):
   - Blended pricing v1 (sheet) with route split assumptions (summary 60%, longform 25%, embeddings 15%)
   - Suggested tiered step-up bands for committed volume (0–10M, 10–50M, 50–150M) that progressively lower $/1M
   - Option: route-level quality SLAs (latency P95) for clinical doc route + minimal fallback routing to cheaper model variants under degraded capacity.

4) Immediate asks from you: confirm whether the 80M/month steady-state is a conservative or optimistic number and whether Nexa will commit to a 6–12 month ramp / minimum. Also confirm procurement owner and target signing date — you mentioned procurement loops in late March.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will attach a versioned blended-price workbook with two scenarios (conservative ramp and aggressive ramp) and Aditya will align on what a blended $/1M looks like if we include a reserved-capacity discount for Dedicated.

If that summary looks right I'll route the pricing worksheet and a short SOW for procurement review.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0123
From: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@nexahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@nexahealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up — token mix & target $/1M for Q3 expansion

Hannah — thanks for the write-up, super helpful. A few clarifications: 

- 80M/mo is our target-case for planning; conservative would be 55–60M/mo and upside could be 120–140M if the pilot shows >15% downstream time savings. So please keep both buckets in the workbook.
- The $950–1,100 per 1M target is on net cost after any reserved capacity discounts — procurement will want to see committed vs. on-demand numbers.
- Procurement lead is Lina (cc'd). Our target signing is end of April but I can push to March 31 if we have final commercial terms and a clean SOW.

Two asks from our side: can you show a blended line-item that separates model type (chat-large, chat-medium, embeddings-quant) with their per-1M and blended total, and also show a scenario where we add the clinical-doc route as a higher-latency SLO (P95 target 300ms) and how that impacts cost?

Also, is there a way to show incremental savings if we quantify prefix caching for repeated documentation templates? That will be an important lever.

Appreciate it — Paul
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@nexahealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Nexa pricing workbook + SOW (v1) — action items and times by owner

Paul / Lina — attaching what we discussed: 1) blended-pricing workbook (scenario tabs: conservative / target / upside), 2) short SOW draft, 3) redline stub for procurement to speed review. Key notes inside the workbook but high level below: 

- Pricing summary (target scenario): blended $/1M = $1,020 (based on 80M steady-state, route mix as discussed).
- If Nexa commits to a 12-month volume band with a 50M lower-bound, blended moves to $920/1M (reserved capacity tier applied).
- Route add (clinical-doc longform): modeled at 1.5x token consumption per session vs. current chat route; we show both same-SLA and uptime+latency-prioritized variants.
- Prefix/KV cache estimate: for repetitive documentation templates we model a 10–18% token reduction on that route depending on template reuse; savings are in the workbook as scenario deltas.

Requested decisions and owners: 
   - Paul / Lina: confirm which scenario (conservative / target / upside) procurement should budget for and whether Nexa will consider a 12-month commit with a 50M floor. Due: 2026-03-12.
   - Aditya (sales engineer): validate latency SLO feasibility for clinical-doc route and whether Dedicated reserved capacity is required to meet P95 300ms.
   - Marissa (rev ops): produce final commercial sheet and draft term language for the commitment bands; will route to procurement.

Attachments (stubs): pricing workbook: 20260306_nexa_blended-pricing-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW: Nexa_MVP_scope_v1.pdf, redline: redline_SOW_Nexa.docx.

If you agree, I can also send a procurement-friendly one-page summary for Lina to circulate.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-06T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexa pricing workbook + SOW (v1) — action items and times by owner

Quick internal note: Hannah — I validated the P95 300ms target for the clinical-doc route on a Dedicated pool (A100 equivalent) assuming batching <= 8 and KV cache primed. If they go on-hosted shared capacity latency could be 20–40% higher during peak.

Also ran a blended sensitivity: with the 12-month / 50M floor we can reach $905–$925/1M depending on exact route mix (I used conservative 20% embeddings uplift). I'll sync the numbers into Marissa's commercial sheet and flag the reserved capacity SKU options.

I'll be available to hop on a call with Lina next week for procurement technical Qs.

—Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
